findings.description: `total = sum(1 for _ in lines)` iterates `lines` once to count it. The CLI passes an open file object, which is a one-shot iterator. After counting, the `for line in lines` loop at line 54 sees an exhausted file and reads nothing. The output is empty, stats show read=0, and progress shows 0/N. Any generator input behaves the same way.
findings.suggestion: Do not pre-count a single-pass iterable. Either materialise it with `lines = list(lines)` (which costs memory), or rewind the file and count separately in the CLI, or report progress without a total.
findings.title: Counting lines consumes a one-shot iterator, so nothing is processed

findings.description: In the `except LookupTimeout` branch, `return enrich(event, geo)` is missing `await`. `enrich` is now async, so `enrich_one` returns a coroutine object. The sink then receives a coroutine rather than an Event, and `to_json` fails or the output is corrupted. The retry never actually runs, and a 'coroutine was never awaited' warning is emitted. A second timeout can never abort the run, as the docstring promises.
findings.suggestion: Use `return await enrich(event, geo)`, so the retry executes and a second LookupTimeout propagates.
findings.title: Retry returns an un-awaited coroutine instead of an Event
